items.label: f01-omission-policy
items.front: The listing parser silently drops a malformed price bound instead of returning an error. Why is that defensible, and what would change it?
items.back: It follows the module's existing convention - an unknown availability value is treated as absent (listing-search-params.ts:73-77). Silent omission is a policy; a visible validation error would be a NEW contract with tests at the route boundary.

items.label: f03-cart-three-homes
items.front: Where does cart state live in this storefront, and which function centralizes every mutation?
items.back: Spree owns the durable cart record (server actions in lib/data/cart.ts), HTTP-only cookies hold cart id and token, and React Context mirrors the session view. mutateCart sets updating, runs the server action, mirrors result.cart into state, then router.refresh() - or toasts the error.

items.label: f02-parse-is-not-trust
items.front: Name three things the URL filter parser cannot promise, and where each belongs.
items.back: It cannot authorize a customer (route), prove a price range is sensible (query builder), or make the ten-minute-cached catalog response fresh (cache/Spree) - it only drops malformed filters.

choices.text: The event name needed for verification lives inside the JSON body
request.json() is unavailable inside Next.js route handlers
JSON.parse is slow, so verifying first is purely a performance optimization
The signature covers the raw bytes, and unverified input should not be parsed

request.json() is unavailable inside Next.js route handlers
JSON.parse is slow, so verifying first is purely a performance optimization
The signature covers the raw bytes, and unverified input should not be parsed

items.explanation: Missing headers answer 401, an invalid signature answers 401, and only then is the verified text parsed (invalid JSON answers 400).

items.prompt: Why does the parser use Number.isSafeInteger rather than Number.isFinite for ?price_min=9007199254740992?

choices.text: It is finite but above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, so isSafeInteger rejects it
isSafeInteger also rejects 0, which the contract wants to exclude
Number.isFinite does not exist as a static method on Number in Node 22
isFinite would reject it as Infinity, so either check works here

choices: It is finite but above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, so isSafeInteger rejects it
isSafeInteger also rejects 0, which the contract wants to exclude
Number.isFinite does not exist as a static method on Number in Node 22
isFinite would reject it as Infinity, so either check works here

items.explanation: 9007199254740992 is 2^53, one above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. 2^53 itself is exactly representable (the guide's 'cannot represent it exactly' is loose: it is 2^53 + 1 that rounds to it), so integers here are no longer safe: isSafeInteger returns false while isFinite returns true. Swapping in Number.isFinite makes test 2 fail.

true: in JS, $ matches before a final line terminator, so the anchored form is unsafe
true, but only on Windows, where the input arrives ending in CRLF
false: without the m flag, $ matches only at the end of input, so both forms work

choices.text: undefined, because parseInt returns NaN for any string that contains letters
priceMin 12, because parseInt reads the numeric prefix and ignores the rest
A thrown RangeError that the route turned into a 400 response
priceMin 0, because parseInt treats unparseable input as zero

choices: undefined, because parseInt returns NaN for any string that contains letters
priceMin 12, because parseInt reads the numeric prefix and ignores the rest
A thrown RangeError that the route turned into a 400 response
priceMin 0, because parseInt treats unparseable input as zero

items.explanation: A prefix parser answers 'what number starts this string?'; this contract asks 'is the whole string a non-negative integer that Number represents exactly?' - so 12px, 12.9 and ' 12' all used to become 12.

It is dead code, left over from an earlier version of the SDK
It becomes part of the cache key, separating guests from users
The SDK reads it implicitly from the closure scope of the function

items.explanation: Finding F3: check at line 47, await sendEmail, mark at line 90 - a check-then-act window. Mark-after-send is deliberate (failed sends retry) but gives at-least-once, and a restart or second instance forgets the Set entirely.
